records.source: בְּךָֽ־יְהוָ֥ה חָסִ֑יתִי אַל־אֵב֥וֹשָׁה לְעוֹלָֽם׃
records.gloss: In you, YHWH, I have taken refuge; let me not be ashamed forever.
pieces: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I have made {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} my refuge; \q never let me be disgraced.

L.1: In {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I have taken refuge; \q let me not be put to shame forever.

R.1: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I run to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} for safety. \q Never let me be put to shame.

decisions.choice: a psalm without a title
decisions.reason: Psalm 71 has no title, which is rare in Books One and Two. It shares its cries and its enemies with Psalm 70 (compare 71:12-13 with 70:2-3), and some Hebrew manuscripts join the two as one psalm. It is the prayer of someone who has trusted God since birth and is now old (verses 5-6, 9, 17-18).

decisions.choice: Psalm 31:2-4
decisions.reason: Verses 1-3 are close to Psalm 31:2-4, with small differences.

decisions.choice: let me not be ashamed forever: never let my trust be proved empty
decisions.reason: To be put to shame is to be let down after trusting, so that others see the trust was misplaced (25:2-3; 31:2).

decisions.choice: I have made you my refuge
decisions.reason: As in the other psalms, Balanced uses a natural phrase for the verb (chasah).

decisions.choice: I run to you for safety
decisions.reason: Readable gives the picture of running to shelter.

records.heading: Do not leave me now I am old

records.source: בְּצִדְקָתְךָ֗ תַּצִּילֵ֥נִי וּֽתְפַלְּטֵ֑נִי הַטֵּֽה־אֵלַ֥י אָ֝זְנְךָ֗ וְהוֹשִׁיעֵֽנִי׃
records.gloss: In your righteousness rescue me and deliver me; incline to me your ear and save me.
pieces: Because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are just, rescue me and set me free; \q bend down to listen to me, and save me.

L.2: In {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} righteousness rescue me and deliver me; \q incline {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} ear to me and save me.

R.2: You always do what is right, so rescue me and set me free. \q Listen to me and save me.

decisions.choice: your righteousness: your faithfulness in setting things right
decisions.reason: God's righteousness (tsedaqah) is his faithfulness to do what is right for his people, and so to rescue them (31:2). The word comes back in verses 15, 16, 19 and 24.

decisions.choice: incline your ear: listen closely
decisions.reason: The picture is of someone bending down to hear (17:6; 31:3).

decisions.choice: Because you are just (B); You always do what is right, so (R)
decisions.reason: "In" here gives the ground of the plea, so Balanced and Readable say "because".

records.source: הֱיֵ֤ה לִ֨י׀לְצ֥וּר מָע֡וֹן לָב֗וֹא תָּמִ֗יד צִוִּ֥יתָ לְהוֹשִׁיעֵ֑נִי כִּֽי־סַלְעִ֖י וּמְצוּדָתִ֣י אָֽתָּה׃
records.gloss: Be for me a rock of dwelling to come continually; you have commanded to save me, for my rock and my fortress [are] you.
pieces: Be a rock I can live in, a place I can always come to. \q You have given the order to save me, \q since {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} are my crag and my stronghold.

L.3: Be for me a rock of dwelling, to come [to] continually; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have commanded to save me, \q for my rock and my fortress [are] {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

R.3: Be like a house of rock where I can always go to be safe. \q You have given the command to save me. \q You are my rock and my strong fort.

decisions.choice: a rock of dwelling (ma'on)
alternatives: a rock of refuge (ma'oz), as in Psalm 31:3 and some Hebrew manuscripts
decisions.reason: The two Hebrew words differ by one letter. Psalm 31:3 has "a rock of refuge", and some manuscripts read that here too. Either way the rock is a safe place to live.

decisions.choice: to come continually; you have commanded: a hard line
alternatives: a fortified house to save me (Psalm 31:3; the ancient Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The words are short and unusual. As they stand they say the rock is a place he can always come to, and that God has already given the order for his rescue. Psalm 31:3 has "a house of strongholds to save me", and the ancient Greek translation reads this verse in that way.

decisions.choice: my rock and my fortress: names for God's protection
decisions.reason: As in 18:3 and 31:4: a high rock (sela') and a stronghold (metsudah) where no enemy can reach.

records.source: אֱֽלֹהַ֗י פַּ֭לְּטֵנִי מִיַּ֣ד רָשָׁ֑ע מִכַּ֖ף מְעַוֵּ֣ל וְחוֹמֵץ׃
records.gloss: My God, rescue me from [the] hand of [the] wicked, from [the] palm of [one who] acts unjustly and [is] ruthless.
pieces: My God, pull me out of the clutches of the wicked, \q out of the grip of the unjust and the cruel.

L.4: My God, rescue me from [the] hand of [the] wicked, \q from [the] palm of [one who] acts unjustly and [is] ruthless.

R.4: My God, save me from the power of evil people. \q Free me from the hold of people who are cruel and unfair.

decisions.choice: hand, palm: power, grip
decisions.reason: To be in someone's hand or palm is to be in their power (31:16).

decisions.choice: ruthless: harsh, oppressive
decisions.reason: The word (chomets) is used only here; it is related to words for being sour or harsh and to the verb "to oppress" (Isaiah 1:17).

decisions.choice: the wicked, the unjust (B); evil people (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has one wicked person, drawn as a type. Balanced uses "the wicked" and Readable says "people"; Literal keeps the singular.

records.source: כִּֽי־אַתָּ֥ה תִקְוָתִ֑י אֲדֹנָ֥י יְ֝הוִ֗ה מִבְטַחִ֥י מִנְּעוּרָֽי׃
records.gloss: For you [are] my hope, Lord YHWH, my trust from my youth.
pieces: For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are my hope, \q Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}; I have trusted in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} since I was young.

L.5: For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [are] my hope, \q Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, my confidence from my youth.

R.5: Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are the one I hope in. \q I have trusted {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} ever since I was young.

decisions.choice: Lord YHWH: the Lord and the divine name
decisions.reason: Here the title 'Adonai is followed by the divine name, which is then read aloud as "God" so as not to say "Lord" twice. All levels write "Lord GOD", with GOD in capitals standing for the name.

decisions.choice: my trust: the one I rely on
decisions.reason: The word (mivtach) is the object of trust, what a person leans on (40:5).

decisions.choice: Lord
decisions.reason: In address the title is "Lord" at every level here, before the name.

records.source: עָלֶ֤יךָ׀נִסְמַ֬כְתִּי מִבֶּ֗טֶן מִמְּעֵ֣י אִ֭מִּי אַתָּ֣ה גוֹזִ֑י בְּךָ֖ תְהִלָּתִ֣י תָמִֽיד׃
records.gloss: On you I have leaned from [the] womb; from [the] belly of my mother you [are the one who] took me out; in you [is] my praise continually.
pieces: I have leaned on {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} from birth; \q it was {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} who drew me from my mother's body. \q I will praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} without ceasing.

L.6: On {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} I have leaned from [the] womb; \q from my mother's belly {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [are the one who] took me out; \q in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [is] my praise continually.

R.6: I have depended on {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} since the day I was born. \q You helped me come out of my mother's body. \q I will always praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: took me out: brought me out at birth
decisions.reason: The word (gozi) is found only here. It is usually linked with a verb meaning to cut or to pull out, picturing God as the one who drew him from the womb, as in 22:10. The ancient Greek translation has "my protector".
The same picture of trusting God from the mother's womb is in 22:10-11.

decisions.choice: I will praise you (B, R)
decisions.reason: "In you is my praise" means God is the one he always praises; Balanced and Readable say so.

records.source: כְּ֭מוֹפֵת הָיִ֣יתִי לְרַבִּ֑ים וְ֝אַתָּ֗ה מַֽחֲסִי־עֹֽז׃
records.gloss: Like a portent I have become to many, and you [are] my strong refuge.
pieces: To many I have become a sign that makes them wonder, \q but {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are my strong shelter.

L.7: Like a portent I have been to many, \q but {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [are] my strong refuge.

R.7: Many people stare at what has happened to me. \q But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are my strong place of safety.

decisions.choice: a portent: a sign that makes people stop and look
decisions.reason: The word (mofet) is a sign or wonder. It can be a warning of judgment (Deuteronomy 28:46) or a marvel of God's care. Here it may mean that people see his troubles as God's punishment, or that his long life under God's protection amazes them.

decisions.choice: but
decisions.reason: The joining word sets God's protection against what people think of him.

records.source: יִמָּ֣לֵא פִ֭י תְּהִלָּתֶ֑ךָ כָּל־הַ֝יּ֗וֹם תִּפְאַרְתֶּֽךָ׃
records.gloss: My mouth is filled [with] your praise, all the day [with] your splendor.
pieces: My mouth is full of praise for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; \q all day long I speak of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} glory.

L.8: My mouth is filled [with] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} praise, \q all the day [with] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} splendor.

R.8: I am always praising {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q All day long I talk about how wonderful {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are.

decisions.choice: your splendor: your beauty and glory
decisions.reason: The word (tif'eret) is beauty or glory, here the glory of God that he praises.

decisions.choice: I speak of
decisions.reason: The second half has no verb; "speak of" is supplied from "my mouth".

records.source: אַֽל־תַּ֭שְׁלִיכֵנִי לְעֵ֣ת זִקְנָ֑ה כִּכְל֥וֹת כֹּ֝חִ֗י אַֽל־תַּעַזְבֵֽנִי׃
records.gloss: Do not cast me off in [the] time of old age; as my strength fails do not forsake me.
pieces: Do not throw me aside now that I am old; \q do not abandon me as my strength gives out.

L.9: Do not cast me off in [the] time of old age; \q as my strength fails, do not forsake me.

R.9: Do not push me away now that I am old. \q Do not leave me alone when I grow weak.

decisions.choice: old age: the speaker is old
decisions.reason: The prayer is spoken by someone who has trusted God from birth (verse 6) and is now old and gray (verse 18).

decisions.choice: cast me off: throw away as useless
decisions.reason: The verb (shalach in the causative) means to throw away (51:13).

records.source: כִּֽי־אָמְר֣וּ אוֹיְבַ֣י לִ֑י וְשֹׁמְרֵ֥י נַ֝פְשִׁ֗י נוֹעֲצ֥וּ יַחְדָּֽו׃
records.gloss: For my enemies have spoken about me, and those who watch my life have consulted together,
pieces: For my enemies are talking about me; \q those who are waiting to take my life are plotting together,

L.10: For my enemies have spoken about me, \q and those who watch [for] my life have conspired together,

R.10: My enemies talk about me. \q People who want to kill me make plans together.

decisions.choice: watch my life: wait for a chance to kill me
decisions.reason: To watch someone's life is to lie in wait for it (56:7).

decisions.choice: a sentence that runs on
decisions.reason: Their words follow in verse 11, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

records.source: לֵ֭אמֹר אֱלֹהִ֣ים עֲזָב֑וֹ רִֽדְפ֥וּ וְ֝תִפְשׂ֗וּהוּ כִּי־אֵ֥ין מַצִּֽיל׃
records.gloss: saying, God has forsaken him; pursue and seize him, for there is no one delivering.
pieces: and they say, "God has abandoned him. \q Go after him and grab him, \q for no one will save him."

L.11: saying, "God has forsaken him; \q pursue and seize him, \q for there is no one to rescue [him]."

R.11: They say, "God has left him. \q Chase him and catch him! \q No one will save him."

decisions.choice: God has forsaken him: the enemies' reading of his troubles
decisions.reason: His enemies take his weakness in old age as proof that God has left him. The prayer of verses 9 and 18 answers this.

decisions.choice: pursue and seize him: the enemies urge each other on
decisions.reason: The verbs are plural commands, spoken by the enemies to one another.

records.source: אֱ֭לֹהִים אַל־תִּרְחַ֣ק מִמֶּ֑נִּי אֱ֝לֹהַ֗י לְעֶזְרָ֥תִי חֽוּשָׁה׃
records.gloss: God, do not be far from me; my God, to my help hurry.
pieces: God, do not stay far away from me; \q my God, come quickly and help me!

L.12: God, do not be far from me; \q my God, hurry to my help!

R.12: God, do not stay far away. \q My God, hurry and help me!

decisions.reason: The plea joins two cries found elsewhere: "do not be far" (22:12; 38:22) and "hurry to my help" (38:23; 40:14; 70:2).

decisions.choice: hurry: the word as read, not as written
decisions.reason: The written text and the form to be read differ only in spelling; the sense is the same.

records.source: יֵבֹ֣שׁוּ יִכְלוּ֮ שֹׂטְנֵ֪י נַ֫פְשִׁ֥י יַֽעֲט֣וּ חֶ֭רְפָּה וּכְלִמָּ֑ה מְ֝בַקְשֵׁ֗י רָעָתִֽי׃
records.gloss: May they be ashamed, may they come to an end, the accusers of my soul; may they be covered [with] reproach and disgrace, those who seek my harm.
pieces: Let my accusers be put to shame and brought to nothing; \q let those who want to hurt me be wrapped in scorn and dishonor.

L.13: May they be ashamed [and] come to an end, the accusers of my soul; \q may they be wrapped [in] scorn and disgrace, \q those who seek my harm.

R.13: Some people accuse me. Let them be ashamed and destroyed. \q Some people want to harm me. \q Cover them with shame and disgrace.

decisions.choice: the accusers: adversaries who bring charges
decisions.reason: The verb (satan) means to oppose or accuse, as an opponent in court (109:4, 20, 29).

decisions.choice: may they be ashamed: a prayer against enemies
decisions.reason: The verbs are wishes, as in 70:3; "covered" pictures shame worn like clothing (35:26; 109:29).

decisions.choice: my (B); me (R)
decisions.reason: "My soul" (nefesh) here means "me".

records.source: וַ֭אֲנִי תָּמִ֣יד אֲיַחֵ֑ל וְ֝הוֹסַפְתִּ֗י עַל־כָּל־תְּהִלָּתֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And I continually will wait, and I will add to all your praise.
pieces: As for me, I will never stop hoping; \q I will add to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} praise again and again.

L.14: But I will wait continually, \q and I will add to all {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} praise.

R.14: But I will always hope in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q I will keep praising {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} more than ever.

decisions.choice: wait: wait in hope
decisions.reason: The verb (yachal) is to wait with hope and expectation (31:25; 38:16).

decisions.choice: add to all your praise: praise you more and more
decisions.reason: Every new act of rescue adds a new reason to the praise already given.

records.source: פִּ֤י׀יְסַפֵּ֬ר צִדְקָתֶ֗ךָ כָּל־הַיּ֥וֹם תְּשׁוּעָתֶ֑ךָ כִּ֤י לֹ֖א יָדַ֣עְתִּי סְפֹרֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: My mouth will recount your righteousness, all the day your salvation, for not I know numbers.
pieces: My mouth will tell of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} righteousness \q and of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} saving help all day long, \q though they are more than I can count.

L.15: My mouth will recount {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} righteousness, \q all the day {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} salvation, \q for I do not know [their] numbers.

R.15: All day long I will tell how {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do what is right and how {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} save. \q There is too much to count!

decisions.choice: I do not know numbers: they cannot be counted
alternatives: I do not know how to tell them all
I am not a learned man
decisions.reason: The word (seforot) is found only here. It is probably "numbers" or "counts": God's saving acts are too many to number (40:6). Some read it as "writings" or "learning", meaning he has no skill with words.

decisions.choice: though
decisions.reason: The joining word (ki) gives the reason his telling never ends; Balanced and Readable make the link plain.

records.source: אָב֗וֹא בִּ֭גְבֻרוֹת אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה אַזְכִּ֖יר צִדְקָתְךָ֣ לְבַדֶּֽךָ׃
records.gloss: I will come with [the] mighty deeds of [the] Lord YHWH; I will make mention of your righteousness, yours alone.
pieces: I will come and tell of the mighty deeds of the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}; \q I will call to mind {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} righteousness, {{deity_pronoun:yours|Yours}} and no one else's.

L.16: I will come with [the] mighty deeds of the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}; \q I will make mention of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} righteousness, {{deity_pronoun:yours|Yours}} alone.

R.16: I will come and tell about the great things the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} has done. \q I will remind everyone how good and fair {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are, and no one else.

decisions.choice: I will come with the mighty deeds: come to tell of them
alternatives: I will come in the strength of the Lord GOD
decisions.reason: He may mean he will come before God, perhaps to the temple, with the story of God's mighty acts to tell; or that he will go on in the strength those acts give.

decisions.choice: the Lord YHWH
decisions.reason: As in verse 5, the title followed by the divine name.

decisions.choice: make mention: proclaim, call to mind
decisions.reason: The verb (zakar in the causative) means to bring to remembrance, to speak of so that others remember (20:8; 45:18).

records.source: אֱֽלֹהִ֗ים לִמַּדְתַּ֥נִי מִנְּעוּרָ֑י וְעַד־הֵ֝֗נָּה אַגִּ֥יד נִפְלְאוֹתֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: God, you have taught me from my youth, and until now I declare your wonders.
pieces: God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have been teaching me since I was young, \q and I am telling of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} wonders still.

L.17: God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have taught me from my youth, \q and until now I declare {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} wonders.

R.17: God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have taught me ever since I was young. \q And I still tell people about the amazing things {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do.

decisions.choice: your wonders: God's amazing acts
decisions.reason: The word (nifla'ot) is used of God's great acts of rescue, such as the exodus (9:2; 40:6).

records.source: וְגַ֤ם עַד־זִקְנָ֨ה׀וְשֵׂיבָה֮ אֱלֹהִ֪ים אַֽל־תַּעַ֫זְבֵ֥נִי עַד־אַגִּ֣יד זְרוֹעֲךָ֣ לְד֑וֹר לְכָל־יָ֝ב֗וֹא גְּבוּרָתֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And even to old age and gray hair, God, do not forsake me, until I declare your arm to a generation, to all who will come your might.
pieces: Now that I am old and gray, God, do not abandon me, \q not until I have told the generation after me what {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} arm has done, \q and made {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} power known to all who are yet to be born.

L.18: And even to old age and gray hair, God, do not forsake me, \q until I declare {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} arm to [the next] generation, \q {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} might to all who are to come.

R.18: Now I am old and my hair is gray. God, do not leave me. \q Let me first tell the young people how strong {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are. \q Let me tell everyone who comes after me about {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} power.

decisions.choice: your arm: your strength in action
decisions.reason: God's arm is a picture of his power to act and to save (44:4; 77:16).

decisions.choice: to a generation, to all who will come: to those who come after
decisions.reason: "A generation" here is the next one, and "all who will come" are those still to be born (22:31-32; 78:4-6). The old man asks to live until he has passed on what God has done.

decisions.choice: the next (L); after me (B); young (R)
decisions.reason: The sense of "a generation" (m2) is made plain at each level.

records.source: וְצִדְקָתְךָ֥ אֱלֹהִ֗ים עַד־מָ֫ר֥וֹם אֲשֶׁר־עָשִׂ֥יתָ גְדֹל֑וֹת אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים מִ֣י כָמֽוֹךָ׃
records.gloss: And your righteousness, God, [is] to [the] height, who have done great things; God, who [is] like you?
pieces: God, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} righteousness rises as high as the heavens; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have done mighty things. \q God, who is there like {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?

L.19: And {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} righteousness, God, [reaches] to the heights, \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} who have done great things; \q God, who [is] like {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?

R.19: God, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} goodness is higher than the sky. \q You have done great things. \q God, no one is like {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}!

decisions.choice: the height: the heavens
decisions.reason: The word (marom) is the high place, the heavens where God is (7:8; 93:4).

decisions.choice: who is like you: God has no equal
decisions.reason: The question echoes the song at the sea (Exodus 15:11) and 35:10; it expects the answer "no one".

decisions.choice: no one is like you!
decisions.reason: Readable gives the answer the question expects (m2).

records.source: אֲשֶׁ֤ר הִרְאִיתַ֨נִי׀צָר֥וֹת רַבּ֗וֹת וְרָ֫ע֥וֹת תָּשׁ֥וּב תְּחַיֵּ֑ינִי וּֽמִתְּהֹמ֥וֹת הָ֝אָ֗רֶץ תָּשׁ֥וּב תַּעֲלֵֽנִי׃
records.gloss: [You] who have made me see troubles, many and evil, you will turn, you will give me life, and from [the] depths of the earth you will turn, you will bring me up.
pieces: You have made me see many troubles and hard times, \q but {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will bring me back to life, \q and raise me once more out of the deep places of the earth.

L.20: You who have made me see troubles many and evil \q will again give me life, \q and from the depths of the earth {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will again bring me up.

R.20: You have let me go through many hard and painful times. \q But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will make me live again. \q You will lift me up again, as if from deep under the earth.

decisions.choice: me: the words as read, not as written
decisions.reason: Two of the verbs are written with "us" ("made us see", "give us life") but marked to be read with "me", which fits the rest of the psalm and the last verb, "bring me up". The words follow the form to be read.

decisions.choice: you will turn: you will do it again
decisions.reason: "Turn" (shuv) before another verb means to do it again: God will once more give life and lift him up.

decisions.choice: the depths of the earth: the realm of death
decisions.reason: The depths (tehomot) below the earth stand for death and the grave (30:4; 88:7). To be brought up from there is to be rescued from dying.

decisions.choice: as if
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain that the depths are a picture (m3).

records.source: תֶּ֤רֶב׀גְּֽדֻלָּתִ֗י וְתִסֹּ֥ב תְּֽנַחֲמֵֽנִי׃
records.gloss: May you increase my greatness, and you will turn [and] comfort me.
pieces: Make me greater than before, \q and turn to comfort me once more.

L.21: May {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} increase my greatness, \q and turn [and] comfort me.

R.21: Give me even more honor than I had before. \q Comfort me again.

decisions.choice: my greatness: my honor and standing
decisions.reason: The word (gedullah) is greatness or honor; he asks that his standing be restored and increased, against those who say God has left him (verse 11).

decisions.choice: you will turn and comfort me: comfort me again
decisions.reason: As in verse 20, "turn" means to do it again, or to turn toward him.

records.source: גַּם־אֲנִ֤י׀אוֹדְךָ֣ בִכְלִי־נֶבֶל֮ אֲמִתְּךָ֪ אֱלֹ֫הָ֥י אֲזַמְּרָ֣ה לְךָ֣ בְכִנּ֑וֹר קְ֝ד֗וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: I also will praise you with an instrument of harp, your faithfulness, my God; I will make music to you with [the] lyre, Holy One of Israel.
pieces: I in turn will thank {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to the music of the harp; my God, I will praise {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithfulness. \q With the lyre I will play for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \q Holy One of Israel.

L.22: I also will praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} with an instrument of harp, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithfulness, my God; \q I will make music to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} with [the] lyre, \q Holy One of Israel.

R.22: My God, I will play the harp and thank {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} keep {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} promises. \q Holy God of Israel, I will play the lyre and sing to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: harp and lyre: two stringed instruments
decisions.reason: As in 33:2: the kinnor was a light lyre held in the hands; the nevel a larger harp.

decisions.choice: the Holy One of Israel
decisions.reason: This title for God is used often in Isaiah (Isaiah 1:4; 6:3) and only three times in the Psalms (71:22; 78:41; 89:19). It names God as holy, set apart from all, and yet bound to Israel.

decisions.choice: because you keep your promises
decisions.reason: Readable says what God's faithfulness ('emet) means for the speaker.

decisions.choice: Holy God of Israel
decisions.reason: Readable uses "God" so that the title is plain.

records.source: תְּרַנֵּ֣נָּ֣ה שְׂ֭פָתַי כִּ֣י אֲזַמְּרָה־לָּ֑ךְ וְ֝נַפְשִׁ֗י אֲשֶׁ֣ר פָּדִֽיתָ׃
records.gloss: My lips will shout for joy when I make music to you, and my soul, which you have redeemed.
pieces: My lips will ring out with joy as I sing {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} praise, \q and so will my whole self, which {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have set free.

L.23: My lips will shout for joy when I make music to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \q and my soul, which {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have redeemed.

R.23: I will shout for joy as I sing to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q With my whole heart I will sing, because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have rescued me.

decisions.choice: redeemed: set free at a cost
decisions.reason: The verb (padah) is used for buying back a person or a firstborn, and for God's rescue of Israel from Egypt (Deuteronomy 7:8); here it is his rescue of the speaker (31:6).

decisions.choice: my whole self (B); my whole heart (R)
decisions.reason: "My soul" (nefesh) is the whole person.

records.source: גַּם־לְשׁוֹנִ֗י כָּל־הַ֭יּוֹם תֶּהְגֶּ֣ה צִדְקָתֶ֑ךָ כִּי־בֹ֥שׁוּ כִֽי־חָ֝פְר֗וּ מְבַקְשֵׁ֥י רָעָתִֽי׃
records.gloss: Also my tongue all the day will murmur your righteousness, for they are ashamed, for they are abashed, those who seek my harm.
pieces: All day long my tongue will speak of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} righteousness, \q for the people who sought my hurt are ashamed and humbled.

L.24: My tongue also will talk all the day [of] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} righteousness, \q for they are put to shame, for they are abashed, those who seek my harm.

R.24: All day long I will talk about how {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do what is right. \q The people who wanted to hurt me are ashamed and disgraced.

decisions.choice: they are ashamed: as good as done
decisions.reason: The verbs are in the past tense. He speaks of the enemies' defeat as already certain, the answer to his prayer in verse 13.

decisions.choice: murmur: speak over and over
decisions.reason: The verb (hagah) is used of quiet, repeated speaking or musing (1:2; 35:28).
